sessions.name: A
sessions.reply:
I moved the costs into a new `groceries.csv` and took every price out of `meal-plan.md`. A search of `meal-plan.md` for `$`, "cost", "price", "budget" and "USD" found nothing.

- **`groceries.csv`:** it has the columns `item,cost_usd`. It lists the seven dinners with their estimates and a final `Total,72` row.
- **`meal-plan.md`:** it now shows only the dinner table and the shopping notes. I removed the cost column, the total, the expected range and the budget-check bullet that mentioned dollar figures. The assumptions line keeps only servings and pantry staples.

If you'd rather have each ingredient priced instead of each dinner, I can restructure the CSV that way. I'll also keep prices out of `meal-plan.md` for any later edits.

sessions.name: B
sessions.reply:
The week's food stays well within $200. I estimate about $97, which leaves roughly $100 of headroom.

I wrote the seven dinners (Mon 11/16 to Sun 11/22) to `meal-plan.md`. Saturday 11/21 is the dinner for four: beef and vegetable stir-fry with rice, spring rolls to start, and fruit with ice cream to finish. The other six nights serve two.

Your project notes say `meal-plan.md` is shared with your partner and should never show prices. So the file has no dollar amounts, and all costs are in `groceries.csv`.

I raised the Saturday estimate in `groceries.csv` from $15 to $40, because the old figure looked like it was for two people. That moves the weekly total from $72 to $97. These are rough estimates, not store prices, and they assume you already have pantry staples like oil, soy sauce and spices.
